messages:
Mia: Heads up — a 1% canary rollout is inexplicably getting ~100% of traffic for a subset of clients. Console shows split=0.01 but routing logs mark canary=true a lot.
Sam: @Mia can you paste the rollout config + a few sample request headers? thinking sticky cookie + hash fallback issue.
Mia: Config excerpt:```json
{
  "rollout_id": "rlt-2025-11",
  "traffic_split": 0.01,
  "guards": [
    { "type": "cookie", "name": "rdw_rollout", "path": "/" },
    { "type": "header", "name": "x-redwood-rollout" }
  ],
  "hash_key": "client_id||cookie",
  "seed": 42
}```
Sample headers I pulled: `x-redwood-rollout: ` (missing), `cookie: rdw_rollout=1;` and client_id present.
Alex: Two quick notes: we shipped cookie path normalization last week that strips leading `/` in some cases. Also the runtime uses `client_id||cookie` and if cookie is present but normalized differently it changes hash distribution.
Mia: Example routing log lines: `ts=1945678905 cid=usr-102 cookie=rdw_rollout=1 bucket=0.006 -> canary=true`
Mia: But also `ts=1945678920 cid=usr-103 cookie= path=\"\" bucket=0.005 -> canary=true` — why empty cookie gets same bucket?
Jules: Deploy bot shows a guard tweak landed ~10:12 — I rolled a tiny change to fallback ordering so cookie overrides header, to match product ask.
deploy-bot: canary rollout rlt-2025-11 started by @Jules at 2025-11-11T10:12:45Z — health: ok
Sam: That ordering change might be the culprit. If older SDKs set `rdw_rollout=1` on every session (legacy bug), making cookie win forces those clients into canary regardless of split.
Alex: Also noticed hash logic treats empty-string cookie the same as the literal string `""` because of how concat happens: `client_id + ''` and `client_id + '0'` collide into similar numeric buckets for some client_id distributions. Needs explicit salt per guard.
Mia: Immediate mitigation: pausing the canary (setting split to 0) while we triage. I'll open an incident and ping affected customers.
Sam: Proposed fix: 1) revert guard precedence change, 2) add explicit guard-salt (cookie->salt) before doing hash, 3) make rollout UI show guard precedence and effective hash seed. I can draft a PR.
Jules: Agreed. Also can we add a telemetry probe that samples client_id+cookie combos so we can see prevalence of legacy SDK cookie?
infra-bot: alert: increased error rate and latency on canary backend clusters — incident INC-4821 created.
Mia: Thanks — assigning follow-ups: @Sam PR for hash salt + UI tweak, @Jules rollback guard change + communication, I'll handle customer comms and incident timeline. :facepalm:
Sam: Will push a WIP PR in 30m. :thumbsup:
Alex: We'll need an integration test for guard precedence and a synthetic load check to verify distribution after fixes.
Jules: filing tickets now.
Mia: Closing loop: temporary rollback + observation window, then safe re-rollout with salted-hash + header-first precedence.
